a 65-nm LDO with high PSRR, high load current range, and small dropout voltage is presented.
we propose an LDO, implemented in 65-nom CMOS, that achieves high PSRR over a wide frequency and load current range.

a low dropout regulator with very low dropout voltage, high PSRR, small overshoot/undershoot, and large load current range, all of which are critical to the performance of SoCs.
the design of a low-dropout voltage regulator with a high power supply rejection ratio.
the design, implementation, and evaluation of a low-dropout regulator (LDO) featuring >60 dB PSRR over 10 MHz frequency range and 100-m A load current range.

the presented LDO is an excellent candidate for use in SoCs.
the proposed LDO is a very promising candidate for use in high-performance and low-power SoCs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the LDO features very low quiescent current of 2.2 mA, low dropout voltage of less than 100 mV, high PSRR of more than 60 dB over a 10 MHz frequency range and a large load current of 100 mA, and small output voltage ripple of less than 5 mV over a 100-mV load current range.
we are the first to present a high PSRR LDO with an NMOS-based output stage.
this paper presents the first LDO that can achieve >60-dB ripple rejection at 10 MHz and >100-mA load current simultaneously.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adaptive FFRC technique is very effective in improving PSRR, even over a wide load current range.
a high-PSRR LDO can be implemented in a standard digital CMOS process, without any additional process, device, or layout (PDL) options, by means of a simple FFRC technique.
the adaptive FFRC technique can be used as a generic solution to achieve high PSRR for LDOs, especially for those realized in CMOS technology.
